newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent off on bearish U.S oil stock builds.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent off on bearish U.S oil stock builds.

text.p: IPE Brent fell on Wednesday as bearish American Petroleum Institute (API) U.S. oil stock data weighed on the market and the Iran situation receded into the background, traders said.
June Brent was trading 17 cents lower at $17.97 a barrel at 1027 GMT, having also shed 20 cents at the end of Tuesday's session. While May gas oil was $2.25 off at $163 a tonne
The data, released late on Tuesday, showed U.S. crude oil stocks rose 2.97 million barrels to 311.41 million.
On the all-important gasoline front, stocks rose 3.63 million barrels to 199.62 million barrels.
Reformulated gasoline stocks rose 162,000 barrels to 35.11 million barrels.
Distillate stocks were also higher, up 2.59 million barrels at 100.97 million.
Traders said given the bearish portent of the data, the market had held up better than expected.
"I thought with the builds we might see it drop further," one trader said.
He also noted that June's lower opening at $17.93 had left a 12 cent downward gap on the daily chart. "It may well fill it but it's not a very positive sign."

Key support for the June contract was pegged around the $17.75/80 level. Traders said the market would be keeping a close eye on NYMEX crude's progress in ACCESS trading with $19.52/55 regarded as a key support level for the May contract.
Traders said that concerns about the Iran issue had receded into the background, which also accounted for some of the losses.
"The main driving force behind the bounce was the Iran situation which added some 40 to 50 cents, said Tom James at Credit Lyonnais in Singapore. "But now the tension hasn't come to anything."
A U.S-Saudi Arabian intelligence report linking an Iranian government official to a group suspected of the 1996 bombing of a U.S. military compound in Saudi Arabia helped prices higher on Monday.
It came on the heels of a German court's ruling last Friday that Iranian leaders were behind the killing of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin. -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
